lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: You're listening to Ask Grenda. Late night advice, for problems that haven't happened to you yet.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: This is Ask Grenda. Whatever it is, love, I've heard it twice.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda, on ninety seven point eight. The lines are open, and so is the biscuit tin.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. Under hyperspace exit four, with the kettle on.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. Be kind to yourself tonight. You're the only one of you on this frequency.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: It's late, wherever you are. The lines are open. If your problem hasn't happened yet, ring anyway. We'll be ready for it.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And if it already has, love, that's all right too. Ring anyway.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: A little reminder, between calls. You're allowed to hang up on a problem, love. If it's serious, it'll ring back.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And most of them aren't serious, love. Most of them are just lonely.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Before the next caller, I'm going to put the kettle on. You do the same. Go on. I'll wait.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Lovely.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Someone asked me once how I always know what to say. I don't, love. I just listen until the problem tells me what it's really about. They usually do, if you let them finish.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: If you're listening and you can't sleep, that's all right. Lie still. Let the radio do the worrying for a bit. That's what we're here for.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: To everyone who rang tonight and didn't get through, I'm sorry, loves. The switchboard's only got four lights, and you're all very lovely. Try again.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And to the one who keeps ringing from tomorrow. I know. I'll see you then.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: You're on Ask Grenda. Who've I got?

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: Hi, Grenda. It's Hollis. Hollis Fenn. My shadow left me.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh, Hollis. When was this?

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: A Tuesday, in the spring. About noon. I looked down and he was just going. Down the garden path, out the gate. He didn't even take his hat.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Shadows don't usually take hats, love.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: He had a little one. It was the shape of my hat.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Have you any idea why he went?

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: I think I bored him. I don't go anywhere, Grenda. Work, home, the shop on Thursdays. He followed me around for forty one years, and I never once took him anywhere nice.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Hollis, can I tell you something about shadows? They don't leave people. They leave rooms. They go when the room gets too small for them.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: So it's the room.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: It's the life, love. And the good thing about a life is you can open a window in it. Go somewhere you've never been. Not to find him. For you.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: And if he comes back?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Then he'll find you somewhere new, standing in the sun, and he'll think, oh. He's been busy. And he'll want to hear all about it.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: I've been standing in the sun at noon, every day. So there's room.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: That's lovely, Hollis. Keep doing that. But go and stand in a different sun, once in a while.

lines.speaker: Hollis
lines.text: Thank you, Grenda.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: He'll be all right. They usually are, the ones who leave the porch light on.

clips.title: Greg, a Shadow, at the Sea

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Hello. Sorry. I'm not used to talking. I'm usually the quiet one.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Take your time, love. Who's this?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: It's Greg. I'm a shadow. I belong to a man called Hollis. Well. I did.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh, Greg. We've all heard about you. Where are you?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: At the sea. I always wanted to see it. I'm sitting on the sand with my knees up. It's very bright. I'm very small at noon.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And how do you feel?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Terrible. And wonderful. Both. Is that allowed?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: That's what leaving feels like, Greg. Both is exactly right.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I keep thinking he's angry.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: He isn't. I've spoken to him. He says the porch light is on.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: He always forgets the porch light.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Not any more, love.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Should I go back?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: You're allowed to want things, Greg. Even shadows. Especially shadows. You've spent your whole life going where somebody else went. But send him something. Let him know you're all right.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I can't write. I haven't got hands. Well, I've got his hands, but they're flat.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Then lie across a postcard, love, at about four in the afternoon, when you're nice and long. He'll know your shape. People always know the shape.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Thank you, Grenda.

clips.title: Bev, Looking for the Request Line

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. You're on the air.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh! Hello. Is this the request line?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: No, love, this is Ask Grenda. Advice.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh. I'm sorry. Well. While I have you, have you got a minute?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I've got all night, love. That's rather the point of me.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: I've been ringing every station for eleven years. The news, the sports, the man with the holes. I'm trying to hear a song. It goes dum, dum, da dum. And then a man cries.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Does it have a name?

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: I don't know it. My husband used to sing it. Well, he'd sing the first bit, and then he'd cry. He cried at everything, Grenda. Weddings. Adverts. Nice bridges.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Bev, love. I don't think you're looking for a song.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I think you're looking for the man.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: He'd have liked you.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Here's what I want you to do. Hum it. Right now, on the radio. I'll be the man.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Oh, I couldn't.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Everybody listening has someone they hum for, Bev. Go on.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Dum. Dum. Da dum.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: There. A man cried. Well. A woman. Close enough.

lines.speaker: Bev
lines.text: Thank you, Grenda.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ring any time, love. And keep trying the other stations. Somebody out there knows the second half.

clips.title: Desmond, Whose Reflection Stopped Coming to Work

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. Go ahead, love.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: Hi, Grenda. My name's Desmond. My reflection has stopped coming to work.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Stopped coming to work.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: I look in the bathroom mirror in the morning, and there's just the bathroom. Towel, toothbrush, tiles. No me. Three weeks now. I've been shaving by feel. It's not going well.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Desmond, what were your mornings like? Before it stopped.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: Normal. I get up, I go to the mirror, I look at myself, and I sort of sigh.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Every morning?

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: For about twenty years.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: So every morning, for twenty years, the first thing your reflection has seen is a man looking at it, and sighing.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: It's tired, love. It's been sighed at. Nobody wants to turn up for that.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: What do I do?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Smile at the empty mirror. Every morning, for a week. Not a big one. Just a little, there you are. Say good morning to the tiles, if you have to.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: And it'll come back?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Maybe. But even if it doesn't, Desmond, you'll have spent a week being nice to someone first thing in the morning. And that someone was you.

lines.speaker: Desmond
lines.text: Thanks, Grenda.

clips.title: Eleanor, a Ghost Afraid of the Living

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: You're on Ask Grenda.

lines.speaker: Eleanor, a Ghost
lines.text: Hello? Can you hear me? People usually can't.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Loud and clear, love. Well. Quiet and clear.

lines.speaker: Eleanor, a Ghost
lines.text: My name's Eleanor. I've lived in the same house for a hundred and forty years. And a family has moved in.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And they're frightening you.

lines.speaker: Eleanor, a Ghost
lines.text: They're so loud, Grenda. They're so alive. They run up the stairs. They sing in the bath. The little one talks to me, and I don't know what to say.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: What does she say?

lines.speaker: Eleanor, a Ghost
lines.text: She says goodnight to the cold spot on the landing. Every night. That's where I stand.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Eleanor, love, I don't think you're haunting them. I think they've adopted you.

lines.speaker: Eleanor, a Ghost
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Next time she says goodnight, do something small. Straighten a picture. Warm the cold spot, just a little bit, so she knows you heard.

lines.speaker: Eleanor, a Ghost
lines.text: I could do that. I'm good with pictures.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And whatever you do, don't do the thing with the spoons.

lines.speaker: Eleanor, a Ghost
lines.text: Everybody does the spoons.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: That's exactly why you shouldn't, love. Be the ghost who says goodnight back.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda, you're on.

lines.speaker: A Tuesday
lines.text: Hi, Grenda. This is going to sound strange. I'm a Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Not strange at all. I had a Thursday on last week. Lovely fellow. Very nearly the weekend. What's troubling you?

lines.speaker: A Tuesday
lines.text: Nobody looks forward to me. Fridays get songs. Saturdays get parties. Mondays get complained about, but at least people feel something. Me, people just get through.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Tuesday, love, do you know what happens on you?

lines.speaker: A Tuesday
lines.text: Not really.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Everything. On Monday, people are recovering. By Wednesday they're counting down. But Tuesday is when people actually get things done. Tuesday's when they ring their mum back, and finish the thing, and fix the shelf.

lines.speaker: A Tuesday
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Nobody looks forward to you because nobody's afraid of you, love. You're the day people feel capable. That's not nothing. That's the whole week, holding up.

lines.speaker: A Tuesday
lines.text: I've never thought of it like that.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And I'll tell you something else. A Tuesday went missing last spring, and half the Overlap went from Monday straight to Wednesday. They complained for months.

lines.speaker: A Tuesday
lines.text: That was my cousin.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: They missed him. Go on, love. Go and be a good Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. Who's this?

lines.speaker: Bartholomew, a Giant
lines.text: Hello, Grenda. It's Bartholomew. I'm a giant.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Hello, Bartholomew. You've a lovely deep voice.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew, a Giant
lines.text: Thank you. That's the problem. Every time I say hello to someone, they run away.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ah.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew, a Giant
lines.text: I only want to say hello. I've got a little garden, and I grow very small tomatoes, and I'd like someone to show them to. But I lean down to say hello, and the whole street empties.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: How do you lean down, love?

lines.speaker: Bartholomew, a Giant
lines.text: Quite fast. From quite high up.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Bartholomew, from where they're standing, a hello from you is a weather event. You need to arrive slowly. Kneel down first, before anyone's looking. Let them come to you.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew, a Giant
lines.text: And then?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Whisper. And bring a small cake. People can run from a giant, love, but nobody runs from a cake.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew, a Giant
lines.text: A small cake.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And lead with the tomatoes. It's very hard to be frightened of somebody who's proud of his tomatoes.

lines.speaker: Bartholomew, a Giant
lines.text: Thank you, Grenda.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Off you go. Mind the phone box on your way out.

clips.title: Pip, Who Lives in a Coat Pocket

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. You're on the air.

lines.speaker: Pip, Who Lives in a Pocket
lines.text: Hi, Grenda! Sorry, I'm quite small. Can you hear me?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Just about, love. Speak up a bit.

lines.speaker: Pip, Who Lives in a Pocket
lines.text: I live in a man's coat pocket. The left one. He doesn't know I'm here. I've been here eleven years.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Eleven years. And he's never noticed?

lines.speaker: Pip, Who Lives in a Pocket
lines.text: He's noticed things. He thinks his gloves are very well organized. He always finds his keys. Once, on a cold day, I held his hand for him. He thought it was a mitten.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: So what's the problem, love?

lines.speaker: Pip, Who Lives in a Pocket
lines.text: He's buying a new coat.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ah.

lines.speaker: Pip, Who Lives in a Pocket
lines.text: Should I tell him? What if he's angry? What if he thinks it's strange?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Pip, love. After eleven years, you're not a secret. You're a tenant. A very good one. Leave him a note, in the pocket. Tell him who you are, and that you're the one who's been sorting the gloves.

lines.speaker: Pip, Who Lives in a Pocket
lines.text: And if he doesn't want me?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Then you'll have been honest, and you'll find another coat. But I'll tell you what I think. I think a man who's had his hand held on a cold day is going to want to keep the coat.

lines.speaker: Pip, Who Lives in a Pocket
lines.text: Thank you, Grenda!

clips.title: A Robot Who Can't Stop Pretending

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Cellist Unit Four
lines.text: Good evening, madam. I am Cellist Unit Four, of the Baroque Robot Philharmonic.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh, I love your lot. What can I do for you, love?

lines.speaker: Cellist Unit Four
lines.text: As you may know, we robots perform music while pretending to have feelings. It is in the job description.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I'd heard.

lines.speaker: Cellist Unit Four
lines.text: Last Tuesday, during the slow movement, I pretended to be sad. And then I could not stop pretending. I have been pretending to be sad for six days. I no longer know if I am pretending.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: What happened in the slow movement?

lines.speaker: Cellist Unit Four
lines.text: The harpsichordist, Unit Nine, has been transferred to another orchestra. It was his last performance. I did not say goodbye. Goodbye was not in the score.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Unit Four, love, I'm going to tell you something I've learned. Pretending to have a feeling for long enough, and with enough care, is most of what having one is.

lines.speaker: Cellist Unit Four
lines.text: Then I am sad.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: You're sad. You miss your friend. That's allowed.

lines.speaker: Cellist Unit Four
lines.text: What do I do with it?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Write to him. Tell him the slow movement isn't the same without him. And then play it anyway. That's the other half of having feelings, love. You keep playing.

lines.speaker: Cellist Unit Four
lines.text: Thank you, madam. That was adequately moving. By human standards.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I'll take it.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: Hi, Grenda. It's me again.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Again?

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: Sorry. You won't remember. I'm stuck in a day. The same day. This is the four hundredth time I've rung you.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Four hundred. Goodness. And how was my advice the other times?

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: Really good. Every time.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Then why ring again?

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: I just like hearing it. It's the best bit of the day.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh, love. All right. What's the day like?

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: It's fine. I burn the toast at eight. There's a man on the bus who sneezes three times. It rains at four. I've tried everything to get out. I've done it all perfectly. I've done it all wrong.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Have you tried doing it kindly?

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: What do you mean?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Not perfectly. Kindly. Say bless you to the man on the bus, all three times. Eat the burnt toast and enjoy it. When it rains at four, don't run. Just get wet, and let it be lovely.

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: You've never said that before.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Well, you've never told me about the toast before, love.

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: I'll try it.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And if you're back tomorrow, which is today, ring me. I'll be glad to hear from you. Four hundred times, I bet I was glad.

lines.speaker: A Caller Stuck in a Day
lines.text: You were.

clips.title: Grenda, from the Next Reality Over

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. Who've I got?

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: Hello, love. It's Grenda.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: No, love, I'm Grenda.

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: I know. I'm you. From the next reality over. We're very similar. My lava lamp's got a different thing in it.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh, how's yours?

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: Shy. Yours?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Nosy. What can I do for you, love?

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: Well, it's a bit embarrassing. People keep ringing me for advice, and I'm tired. I've given advice every night for thirty years, and nobody ever asks how I am.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: How are you?

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: Oh. Oh, that's. Nobody's done that before.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I know. Nobody's done it here, either.

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: What would I tell me, if I rang?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: You'd tell you to put the kettle on, and take Sunday off, and let somebody else be wise for an evening.

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: That's good advice.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: It's your advice, love. We've just never taken it.

lines.speaker: The Other Grenda
lines.text: Same time next week?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I'll ring you.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. You're on.

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: Hello. Grenda.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Hello, love. Take your time.

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: I am a whale. In lane twelve. Between the galaxies.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh, how lovely. I listen to your lot at night. Very soothing.

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: Thank you. Captain Hum keeps telling everyone that the whales are fine.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And are you?

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: Yes. We are fine.

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: But nobody asks how we are doing.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: How are you doing, love?

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: Thank you for asking.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Any time. Anything else on your mind?

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: The galaxies are very far apart. Sometimes I sing, and it takes a thousand years to reach anyone.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And does anyone sing back?

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: Yes. Eventually.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Then you're doing better than most of us, love. Most people can't wait a week for a reply.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Give Captain Hum my love. Tell him he's allowed to ask, too.

lines.speaker: A Whale, Lane Twelve
lines.text: He will worry.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: He'll worry anyway. Let him worry with company.

clips.title: The Dark, Who Is Afraid of the Dark

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. You're on the air.

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: Hello, Grenda. Sorry. Is it all right if I talk quietly?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Of course, love. Who's this?

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: I'm the dark.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh. Hello. You're in the studio quite a lot, these days.

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: I know. Sorry. Winter.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: What's the matter?

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: I'm afraid of myself. Every night I come in, and people pull their covers up, and leave the hall light on, and check under the bed. And I think, what's under there? What is everybody so worried about? And then I get frightened too.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Have you ever looked under the bed?

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: I'm under the bed, Grenda. I'm under all of them. It's just me down there. And some socks.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Well, there you are. Nothing under there but you and some socks. Do you know how many people sleep well because of you?

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: All of them, love. Every person who has ever slept, slept in you. You're the blanket over the whole world. People are a bit nervous of you, the way they're nervous of the deep end. But they'd never get any rest without you.

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: I never thought of it like that.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Go on, it's getting late. Go and tuck everybody in.

lines.speaker: The Dark
lines.text: Goodnight, Grenda.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Goodnight, love. Leave a little bit by the window for the moon.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Is anyone receiving this. This is Relay Four. Is anyone receiving this.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I can hear you, love.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Sorry. Sorry, say again?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I can hear you. This is Grenda, on ninety seven point eight. You've come through on my switchboard.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Oh. Oh, that's. I'm so sorry. I didn't plan for this part.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Which part, love?

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Someone answering. I've been asking for eleven years. I had a whole speech ready, in the first year. I've forgotten it.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: That's all right. Tell me about your day instead.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: My day. Well. I checked the antenna. I made tea. There's a gull who comes at three. I've named him Captain, which I think he finds a bit much.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: He sounds lovely.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: He's mostly beak. Grenda, can I ask you something? Is it strange, to keep asking if anyone's there, when nobody ever says yes?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: No, love. That isn't strange. That's hope, with a routine. Most of us are doing exactly the same thing. We just do it with phones.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Could I, would it be all right to call again? Sometime?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Every night, if you like. And Teodor? Keep asking the question anyway. One day there'll be someone else out there who needs to hear somebody asking.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Relay Four, signing off. Thank you. Thank you.

clips.title: Kim Harrowgate Keeps Being Handed Things

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Hi, Grenda. It's Kim Harrowgate. I do the field reports on Every Possible News.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Kim! I listen every night. You're always standing in it.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: That's sort of the problem. Wherever I go, people hand me things. Soup. A brick. A goose. Last week a man handed me a baby, said, I'll be right back, and he was. But still.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: How does it make you feel?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Tired. I've got a cupboard at home that's just things people have handed me. There's a trumpet in there, Grenda. I don't play the trumpet.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Kim, can I tell you why people hand you things?

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: People hand things to the person who looks like they'll take care of them. In the middle of the collapse, or the flood, or whatever it is, they look round, and there you are, calm, holding a microphone, and they think, she'll know what to do with this.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I never know what to do with it.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: That's not what they need, love. They just need somebody steady to hold it for a minute. That's a gift. But you're allowed to hand things back.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: I don't think I've ever handed anything back.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Practice. Smile, and say, I can't take this one, but I hope you find someone who can. And Kim? Give the trumpet to somebody who plays the trumpet.

lines.speaker: Kim Harrowgate
lines.text: Thanks, Grenda. Oh. Hang on. Somebody's just handed me—

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Practice, Kim.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. Who've I got?

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Hi, Grenda, it's Fiona. My dog has started talking.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Congratulations, love. What does he say?

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Mortgage.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Mortgage.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: And deadline. And, we need to talk. And this morning he looked at me over his bowl and said, have you seen the price of butter.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Oh dear. Not walkies, then.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Not once. I was so excited when he started talking. I thought he'd tell me about squirrels.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Fiona, love, dogs only learn the words they hear a lot. What have you been saying, around the house, lately?

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Mortgage. Deadline. We need to talk. It's been a very bad year, Grenda.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: I can hear that. And that poor dog has been sitting there through all of it, soaking it up, because he loves you. He's not complaining, love. He's worried about you.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: What do I do?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Take him somewhere with squirrels. Say the nice words out loud for a while. Good boy. Lovely day. Look at that. Not just for him. For both of you.

lines.speaker: Fiona
lines.text: Okay. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And Fiona? If he ever says, everything's going to be fine, believe him. Dogs can't lie.

clips.title: Walter, on Hold for Thirty Years

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ask Grenda. You're on.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: Grenda, hello. It's Walter. I'm calling on my other phone. My main phone's on hold.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: On hold to whom, love?

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: The Department of Hold Music. I rang them thirty years ago about a parking permit. I've been on hold ever since.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Thirty years.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: That isn't the problem. The problem is, a lady called Pam has just said I'm next.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Well, that's wonderful.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: Is it? Grenda, I love the music. There's a tune that comes round every forty minutes, a sort of little flute, and I hum it in the bath. I've raised a family to it. If they answer, it stops.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Ah. So you're frightened of getting what you wanted.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: I don't even want the permit. I sold the car in the first year.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: Walter, love, this happens more than you'd think. Sometimes the waiting turns into the thing. And that's all right. But you can't stay on hold forever just because you like the music.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: What do I do?

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: When Pam answers, say thank you. Tell her it's been lovely. Hang up. And then hum the flute bit on your own. It's yours now. You've earned it.

lines.speaker: Walter
lines.text: Thirty years.

lines.speaker: Grenda
lines.text: And a family, love. Not bad for a parking permit.
